source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - framework
finding: ToT frames a problem as search over a tree of thoughts. Four design questions: how to split thoughts, how to generate them, how to evaluate states, which search to use. IO, CoT, CoT-SC and self-refine are special cases of ToT.
numbers: Thought size: a few words (crosswords), one equation (Game of 24), a paragraph plan (writing). Tests run May 5-16 2023 with GPT-4.
limits: Authors call it a modern version of A*-style heuristic search where the LM supplies the heuristic. Only BFS and DFS tried; A* and MCTS left for future work.
agent_relevance: Good map for S6: a thought must be small enough to vary, big enough to judge. Our idea tree needs the same choice.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - generators and evaluators
finding: Two ways to generate: i.i.d. samples from a CoT prompt (rich thought space) or a sequential propose prompt (small space, avoids duplicates). Two ways to evaluate: value each state alone (sure/maybe/impossible or 1-10) or vote across states.
numbers: Value prompts sampled 3 times per thought in Game of 24; 5 votes per step in Creative Writing; 5 proposal prompts in crosswords.
limits: Evaluation uses lookahead simulation plus commonsense (too big or small to reach 24).
agent_relevance: Matches G5: compare siblings in code where possible; model votes only when no check exists.
quote: such valuations do not need to be perfect, and only need to be approximately helpful for decision making

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - Game of 24
finding: Main result. GPT-4 IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC (k=100) 9.0%, IO+Refine (k=10) 27%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%.
numbers: 100 hard games, indices 901-1000 of 4nums.com (1,362 games). IO and CoT averaged over 100 samples each. Refine uses ground-truth feedback. ToT is BFS, 3 steps, keep b=5. Oracle best-of-100: IO 33%, CoT 49%.
limits: Baselines not matched in compute. Test games are the hard end of the list.
agent_relevance: Search with pruning beat sampling on this task. Check compute match before trusting the gap.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - Game of 24 error analysis
finding: About 60% of CoT samples already fail after the first step (the first three words, e.g. 4 + 9). Left-to-right decoding commits early and cannot recover.
numbers: Figure 3b, failure by step, CoT vs ToT b=5; value read from text.
limits: Shows the gain comes from early pruning where the first choice matters.
agent_relevance: Supports branching at the first decision point of S6, not late.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - cost
finding: ToT uses 5.5k completion tokens per Game of 24 case, close to 100 CoT trials (6.7k). Cost per case: IO best-of-100 $0.13 (33%), CoT best-of-100 $0.47 (49%), ToT $0.74 (74%). Creative Writing: ToT about 5x cost of CoT.
numbers: Appendix B.3. Main runs cost about $106 total. Authors say ToT can need 5-100x more generated tokens than CoT.
limits: Table text is garbled in the PDF; method-to-cost pairing inferred from column order and the stated $0.74.
agent_relevance: Budget in the loop: expect large multiples of CoT cost; use a tree only where CoT fails.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - Creative Writing
finding: GPT-4 coherence score (1-10): IO 6.19, CoT 6.93, ToT 7.56. Humans preferred ToT over CoT in 41 of 100 pairs, CoT over ToT in 21, 38 similar. Iterative refine lifted IO to 7.67 and ToT to 7.91.
numbers: 100 inputs of 4 random sentences; ToT depth 2, 5 plans then vote, 5 passages then vote, 5 votes each, b=1. Judge GPT-4 (5 scores averaged, SD about 0.56).
limits: Judge is the same model family as the generator. Human raters were a subset of the authors. No ground truth.
agent_relevance: Self-judged gains are weak evidence; matches G5 warning about model judges.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - Mini Crosswords
finding: ToT reaches 78% letters, 60% words, 20% games (4 of 20); IO and CoT stay under 16% words. Oracle best state 82.4 / 67.5 / 35%. No pruning 65.4 / 41.5 / 5%. No backtracking 54.6 / 20 / 5%.
numbers: 20 test games (1,6,...,96) of 156 from goobix.com; DFS capped at 100 steps; IO and CoT 10 samples each.
limits: Pruning heuristic is imperfect: GPT-4 treated obsolete words like 'agend' as typos. Unpruned search found 4/20 solutions, 3 that pruned ToT missed.
agent_relevance: Backtracking and pruning each matter, but bad pruning discards true solutions. Keep dropped branches recoverable (S6).
quote: better heuristics for DFS pruning are critical for problem solving in this case

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - weaker model and easy tasks (appendix B.1-B.2)
finding: GPT-3.5 Game of 24: IO 6%, CoT 3%, ToT 19% (GPT-4 74%). GPT-4 generating with GPT-3.5 evaluating: 64%. GPT-3.5 generating with GPT-4 evaluating: 31%. GPT-3.5 Creative Writing: IO 4.47, CoT 5.16, ToT 6.62. Zero-shot ToT on easy tasks: GSM8K CoT 86 to ToT 90; StrategyQA CoT 82 to ToT 83.
numbers: GSM8K and StrategyQA: 100 random questions each. GPT-3.5 needed a 3-shot propose prompt instead of 1-shot.
limits: Table columns were mixed in the PDF text; GSM8K/StrategyQA values read from layout. Gains on easy tasks are small.
agent_relevance: Bottleneck on Game of 24 is generation, not evaluation. Use the strong model to propose; a cheap model can judge.

source: Long (2023) Large Language Model Guided Tree-of-Thought
finding: Independent, near-simultaneous ToT with a rule-based checker, memory module and controller that backtracks when the checker rejects a board or after 5 children. Sudoku: ToT solved all ten 3x3, 9 of 10 4x4, 8 of 10 5x5.
numbers: gpt-3.5-turbo, temperature 1, 10 puzzles per size, max 100 conversation rounds. One-shot and few-shot reach about 0.5 on 4x4 and 5x5; ToT is 80% and 60% higher relative.
limits: Tiny samples (10 per size). Weak model. Checker and controller are code, so the search is not LLM-judged. Bar heights read from a figure.
agent_relevance: Closest to our design: code checker decides, model fills a slot. A code-controlled tree works on constraint puzzles.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: MCTS where the LLM is also the world model. Blocksworld success with LLaMA-33B: RAP(10) 100% at 2 steps, 86% at 4, 26% at 6; RAP(20) 100 / 88 / 42%. CoT solves only a few 2-step cases. GSM8k: CoT+SC(10) 46.8, RAP(10) 48.6, RAP aggregate 51.6. ProntoQA proof accuracy: CoT 64.8, RAP 78.8.
numbers: Blocksworld 30/57/114 cases at 2/4/6 steps. Reward mixes likelihood, self-evaluation and task heuristics. Llama-2 70B on full Blocksworld: CoT near 0 beyond 6 steps, RAP higher.
limits: Concurrent with ToT; tasks and models differ. Task-specific reward helps Blocksworld. Some GSM8k row labels were garbled in the PDF text.
agent_relevance: Tracking an explicit state (world model) before judging helps deep plans; relevant to S6 state notes.

source: Xie et al. (2023) Self-Evaluation Guided Beam Search for Reasoning
finding: Step-level beam search with LLM self-evaluation. Codex: GSM8K 85.5 vs 80.4 for the PAL baseline, AQuA 64.2 vs 58.6, StrategyQA 77.2 vs 73.2. Equal-cost test on Llama-2 13B: 46.1% at 12.6k tokens vs self-consistency 41.8% at 13.9k.
numbers: Gains are small where the baseline is strong (Object Counting baseline 96.7%). Slightly below plain CoT on short commonsense chains (StrategyQA 70.6 vs 71.0; CommonsenseQA 74.0 vs 74.4).
limits: Best on long, diverse chains. High-confidence tasks leave little search space.
agent_relevance: Step search pays on long chains; skip it on short ones.

source: Sel et al. (2023) Algorithm of Thoughts
finding: One-query imitation of tree search inside the prompt. Game of 24 GPT-4: AoT 71% with 1 query vs ToT b=5 69% with 109.1 queries. Mini crossword word success: AoT 52% (2 queries), ToT 46.5% (over 200 queries), CoT-SC 15.6%.
numbers: Same task splits as Yao. Game of 24 prompt tokens: AoT 5,450 vs ToT 13,900; completion 998 vs 5,500. Crossword tokens about 25x lower than ToT.
limits: Their ToT reproduction gave 69% on Game of 24 (original 74%) and 46.5% on crossword words (original 60%). Setups may differ.
agent_relevance: Search behaviour can be placed in one long prompt with in-context DFS traces; cheaper than many calls.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Reasoning in Token Economies: Budget-Aware Evaluation of LLM Reasoning Strategies
finding: At equal budget, self-consistency matches or beats MAD and Reflexion on most datasets. ToT on Game of 24: with GPT-4, ToT beats CoT-SC by a big margin even budget-matched; with GPT-3.5, CoT-SC beats ToT by a considerable margin.
numbers: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4; CoT-SC up to 100 samples. GPT-4 ToT ablation: a random evaluator gives a steep drop; a GPT-3.5 evaluator with GPT-4 proposer, and one evaluation instead of three, were also tested.
limits: Exact accuracies only in figures, not recorded. GPT-3.5 evaluator prompt was modified, a tuning confound. One task for ToT.
agent_relevance: Replication with a boundary: ToT needs a strong proposer and a good evaluator. Random pruning removes most of the gain.
quote: A strong model is needed to perform better than baseline

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) On the Self-Verification Limitations of LLMs on Reasoning and Planning Tasks
finding: GPT-4 as verifier on Game of 24 (4100 judgements, instances 1-1000): accuracy 87.0%, false positive rate 10.4% (320/3071), false negative rate 20.7% (213/1029). It marks 79.1% of correct 24-expressions as correct but evaluates 81.6% of them to 24.
numbers: Blocksworld verifier accuracy 72.4%, Mystery Blocksworld 71.8%. A sound verifier (SymPy) in the loop fixes the problem; LLM self-critique does not.
limits: Bears on the evaluator half of ToT: state-value errors can prune true paths. GPT-4 of early 2024.
agent_relevance: Supports G5 and G2: use code checks to score thoughts where possible.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without oracle labels, GPT-3.5 self-correction lowers accuracy: CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 (round 1) and 41.8 (round 2); GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7; HotpotQA 26.0 to 25.0. With oracle labels it rises (GSM8K 75.9 to 95.5).
numbers: GPT-3.5 kept its first GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time; when it changed, correct-to-wrong exceeded wrong-to-correct. GSM8K: self-consistency (6) 85.3 vs multi-agent debate 83.2.
limits: A different loop from ToT, but the same weakness: the model judges its own text poorly. Earlier gains came from oracle feedback.
agent_relevance: Supports G2: no revision from model opinion; use real outputs.

source: Mo and Xin (2023) Tree of Uncertain Thoughts Reasoning for LLMs
finding: Adds Monte Carlo sampling variance as an uncertainty signal to ToT value estimates. Reports gains over ToT of 5% (b=1) and 9% (b=5) on Game of 24, and 2/4/3 points on crossword letters/words/games. Best at 20 Monte Carlo steps; 50 or 100 no better.
numbers: Sampling steps tested {5,10,20,50,100}. Game of 24 table cells were garbled, so only text claims recorded.
limits: Small arXiv paper, not peer reviewed in this record. Baseline ToT numbers may differ from Yao's.
agent_relevance: Variance across repeated judgements is a cheap uncertainty hint for pruning.

source: Besta et al. (2024) Graph of Thoughts
finding: GoT beats ToT on decomposable tasks with GPT-3.5: for sorting 128 numbers GoT cuts median errors 62% versus ToT with over 31% lower cost; at 64 numbers its median error is 65% below CoT and 83% below IO.
numbers: Sorting, set intersection, keyword counting, document merging. GPT-3.5 only (Llama-2 tried, worse and slower). ToT usually better than its cheaper variant ToT2 but costs more.
limits: Tasks chosen to be decomposable and merge-friendly. Not the Game of 24 or crossword set.
agent_relevance: Merging partial solutions can beat pure tree search when subtasks combine.

source: Bi et al. (2024) Forest-of-Thought
finding: Game of 24 comparison table: IO 10.22%, CoT 4.38%, CoT-SC 4.38%, GoT 5.26%, ToT b=5 74.00%, BoT 82.40%, XoT 85.40%, FoT 96.84% (25.64 LLM calls vs ToT 13.74).
numbers: Multiple parallel trees, sparse activation, self-correction. Ablation: with correction and input enhancement 77.98%.
limits: Numbers mix sources, not one controlled run. About double the calls of ToT.
agent_relevance: More trees plus a correction step raised the ceiling on this task, at nearly double the calls.

source: Lehnert et al. (2024) Beyond A*: Better Planning with Transformers via Search Dynamics Bootstrapping
finding: A Transformer trained on A* search traces (Searchformer) solves 93.7% of unseen Sokoban puzzles optimally with up to 26.8% fewer search steps than the A* used to train it.
numbers: Needs training; 5-10x smaller model and 10x smaller data than direct-plan baselines.
limits: Training route, not prompting; the opposite of ToT's no-training claim.
agent_relevance: Out of scope for a scaffold-only agent, but shows search can be learned as tokens.

source: Besta et al. (2024) Demystifying Chains, Trees, and Graphs of Thoughts
finding: Survey that defines a taxonomy of reasoning topologies (chain, tree, graph) and places ToT as the tree case with generation, scoring and search parts.
numbers: Survey; no new measurement.
limits: No new numbers; only abstract and intro read.
agent_relevance: Vocabulary for describing our own S6 tree.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - search algorithms
finding: BFS keeps the b best states per step (used when depth is 3 or less, b at most 5). DFS goes to the best state first, prunes when value is under a threshold, then backtracks to the parent.
numbers: Game of 24 and Creative Writing use BFS; crosswords use DFS with a 100-step cap and no overwriting of filled words so depth is at most 10.
limits: Algorithms 1 and 2 in the paper. No A*, MCTS or learned value; search policy is hand-set per task.
agent_relevance: Our S6 needs a per-task choice of breadth and depth set by code, not by the model.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs - breadth effect and ablation summary
finding: Breadth matters: b=1 gives 45% on Game of 24 and b=5 gives 74%. On crosswords removing backtracking drops word success from 60% to 20%, and removing pruning drops it to 41.5%.
numbers: Same runs as Game of 24 and crossword tables.
limits: Ablations on 20 crossword games only; one seed set.
agent_relevance: Both wide beams and the ability to back up are needed; one alone is weaker.

source: Hao et al. (2023) RAP - reward ablation and failure cases
finding: RAP lets LLaMA-33B beat GPT-4 CoT on Blocksworld by 33% relative gain. Case study: the world model holds the current block state, so later steps get an easier sub-problem and more search budget goes to early steps.
numbers: Blocksworld 6-step search space up to 5^6 paths; 42% solved within 20 iterations. Reward ablation in Tables 5 and 6.
limits: Gains depend on task-specific reward; general rewards less helpful.
agent_relevance: Rewrite the state after each step so later judging sees only the current state.

source: Sel et al. (2023) Algorithm of Thoughts - how it works
finding: Prompt examples are DFS traces with false starts and backtracking written out. The model then imitates the search in one pass at temperature 0.
numbers: Game of 24 AoT 71% vs standard CoT 4.0% and CoT-SC 9.0%.
limits: Needs long context; success depends on the examples showing search.
agent_relevance: In-context search traces are a cheaper alternative to external tree calls.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Token Economies - ToT proposer and evaluator split
finding: Splitting ToT cost into proposer and evaluator: the evaluator matters non-trivially. Random pruning steeply cuts accuracy, so the model's self-evaluation carries real signal in GPT-4.
numbers: Game of 24, ToT b=1,3,5 vs CoT-SC b=100, GPT-4 and GPT-3.5.
limits: Numbers only in figures.
agent_relevance: Keep an evaluator that is better than chance; test it against random pruning.
quote: Evaluator quality has a non-trivial impact

source: Stechly et al. (2024) Self-Verification - Game of 24 setup
finding: Used the same 4nums.com data as Yao, instances 901-1000 for generation, 1-1000 for verification, so its numbers can be compared with Yao's.
numbers: GPT-4; tasks Game of 24, Graph Coloring, Blocksworld, Mystery Blocksworld.
limits: Second-hand claim of a mismatch with Yao came from a search snippet, not read; not recorded.
agent_relevance: Reuse test split 901-1000 so our numbers compare with Yao.
